doc.title: John Heard interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Commissioned self-portrait and selling limited-edition art
summary: He is working on a commissioned self-portrait with his bass, avoids galleries and sells editions of ten at reasonable prices.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I don’t have any exhibitions. I just do commissions. So I’m working on myself at the moment. Someone commissioned me to do a self-portrait playing the bass, so I got this up here with the neck and the bass and my hands to here. It’s turning out very nice.
That’s great. You get to do yourself.
I’m ugly, boy. This schnoz, man, I’ll tell you this schnoz is kicking the shit out of me. I like to say that.
Hard to get it down, huh?

There’s so many different little things happening here. But it’s coming. It’s really looking nice. And you know I don’t deal with galleries. People know what I do and they contact me and I sell, at a reasonable price, and they’re getting something that’s probably valuable, you know. I think an art gallery would say it would be pretty valuable. And I only do, when it has on there it’s one of ten, it’s one of ten. Because you can’t get it anyplace else. So that has customers coming back when they know they’re not getting ripped off.
They’ve got something pretty unique, huh?
